arxiv-1801-02460.title: The Gaussian Noise Model in the Presence of Inter-channel Stimulated Raman Scattering
arxiv-1801-02460.creator: Daniel Semrau, and Polina Bayvel
arxiv-1801-02460.description: Abstract A Gaussian noise (GN) model is presented that properly accounts for an arbitrary frequency dependent signal power profile along the link. This enables the evaluation of the impact of inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS) on the optical Kerr nonlinearity.

arxiv-2308-16606.description: Abstract We report an updated measurement of the ν μ \nu_{\mu} -induced, and the first measurement of the ν ¯ μ \bar{\nu}_{\mu} -induced coherent charged pion production cross section on C 12 {}^{12}\textup{C} nuclei in the T2K experiment. This is measured in a restricted region of the final-state phase space for which p μ , π > 0.2 p_{\mu,\pi}>0.

arxiv-2401-12859.title: Some Aspects of Higher Continued Fractions
arxiv-2401-12859.creator: Etan Basser, Nicholas Ovenhouse, Anuj Sakarda
arxiv-2401-12859.description: Abstract We investigate some properties of the higher continued fractions defined recently by Musiker, Ovenhouse, Schiffler, and Zhang. We prove that the maps defining the higher continued fractions are increasing continuous functions on the positive real numbers. We also investigate some asymptotics of these maps.

arxiv-2406-10256.title: Explicit Word Density Estimation for Language Modelling
arxiv-2406-10256.creator: Jovan Andonov
arxiv-2406-10256.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jovan Andonov. Language Modelling has been a central part of Natural Language Processing for a very long time and in the past few years LSTM-based language models have been the go-to method for commercial language modeling. Recently, it has been shown that when looking at language modelling from a matrix factorization point of view, the final Softmax layer limits the expressiveness of the model, by putting an upper bound on the rank of the resulting matrix.

arxiv-2411-05885.title: Alternative Learning Paradigms for Image Quality Transfer
arxiv-2411-05885.creator: \firstname Ahmed Karam \surname Eldaly https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2266-6992 \email A.Karam@ucl.ac.uk, \name Matteo Figini https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8238-2262 \email M.Figini@ucl.ac.uk, \name Daniel C. Alexander https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2439-350X \email D.Alexander@ucl.ac.uk
arxiv-2411-05885.description: Abstract Image Quality Transfer (IQT) aims to enhance the contrast and resolution of low-quality medical images, e.g. obtained from low-power devices, with rich information learned from higher quality images. In contrast to existing IQT methods in the literature which adopt supervised learning frameworks, in this work, we propose two novel formulations of the IQT problem.

arxiv-2412-20991.title: Topological gap solitons in equidistant lithium niobate waveguide arrays
arxiv-2412-20991.creator: Andrey V. Gorbach
arxiv-2412-20991.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Andrey V. Gorbach. Equidistant 1D arrays of thin film lithium niobate waveguides can exhibit non-trivial topology due to a specific interplay between inter- and intra-modal couplings of two families of guided modes Gorbach et al. In this work we analyze two-colour spatial solitons, emerging due to χ 2 \chi_{2} nonlinear interactions between the modes of non-trivial topology in the fundamental harmonic field, and modes of trivial topology in the second harmonic field.

arxiv-2509-11576.title: Reconstructing High-fidelity Plasma Turbulence with Data-driven Tuning of Diffusion in Low Resolution Grids
arxiv-2509-11576.creator: Kunpeng Li, Youngwoo Cho, Xavier Garbet, Chenguang Wan, Robin Varennes, Kyungtak Lim, Virginie Grandgirard, Zhisong Qu, Ong Yew Soon
arxiv-2509-11576.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kunpeng Li, Youngwoo Cho, Xavier Garbet, Chenguang Wan, Robin Varennes, Kyungtak Lim, Virginie Grandgirard, Zhisong Qu, Ong Yew Soon. Developing physically consistent closure models is a longstanding challenge in simulating plasma turbulence, even in minimal systems such as the two-field Hasegawa–Wakatani (HW) model, which captures essential features of drift-wave turbulence with a reduced set of variables.

arxiv-2511-09620.title: Cooling the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model using thermofield double states
arxiv-2511-09620.creator: Thomas Schuster, Bryce Kobrin, Vincent P. Su, Hugo Marrochio, Norman Y. Yao
arxiv-2511-09620.description: Abstract We analyze a simple and efficient experimental protocol to cool the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model to low temperatures. The protocol utilizes local couplings between two copies of an SYK model to create a gapped adiabatic path, between a high temperature product state and a low temperature thermofield double state.

pmc-10674360.title: Eat to Treat: The Methods and Assessments of a Culinary Medicine Seminar for Future Physicians and Practicing Clinicians
pmc-10674360.creator: Kate Donovan, Olivia W. Thomas, Ty Sweeney, Tyler J. Ryan, Sonja Kytomaa, Molly Zhao, Wayne Zhong, Michelle Long, Iniya Rajendran, Suzanne Sarfaty, Carine Lenders
pmc-10674360.description: Nutrition-associated chronic disease is an epidemic in the United States (US), yet most medical schools lack adequate nutrition education. We developed a six-session culinary medicine (CM) seminar entitled “Eat to Treat: A Nutrition Course for Future Clinicians” that teaches culinary skills, nutrition science, and counseling techniques to improve clinical nutrition management.

pmc-11437115.title: Dim light at night unmasks sex-specific differences in circadian and autonomic regulation of cardiovascular physiology
pmc-11437115.creator: Abhilash Prabhat, Dema Sami, Allison Ehlman, Isabel Stumpf, Tanya Seward, Wen Su, Ming C Gong, Elizabeth A Schroder, Brian P Delisle
pmc-11437115.description: Shift work and artificial light at night disrupt the entrainment of endogenous circadian rhythms in physiology and behavior to the day-night cycle. We hypothesized that exposure to dim light at night (dLAN) disrupts feeding rhythms, leading to sex-specific changes in autonomic signaling and day-night heart rate and blood pressure rhythms.

pmc-11467392.title: Nonlinear dynamic modeling and vibration analysis for early fault evolution of rolling bearings
pmc-11467392.creator: Longkui Zheng, Yang Xiang, Ning Luo
pmc-11467392.description: In rotating machinery, the condition of rolling bearings is paramount, directly influencing operational integrity. However, the literature on the fault evolution of rolling bearings in their nascent stages is notably limited. Addressing this gap, our study establishes an innovative nonlinear dynamic model for early fault evolution of rolling bearings based on collision impact.

pmc-11475544.title: Prolonged exposure to a public health event: the mediating role of resilience between social support and post-traumatic growth among frontline nurses
pmc-11475544.creator: Dejian Zeng, Yan Li, Caixia Yang, Dan Tang, Yanzhi Yi, Yanjun He, Mingyan Yang
pmc-11475544.description: Background Inthe early days of December 2022, the Chinese government ended its restrictive quarantine measures (e.g. nationwide lockdown) against COVID-19, which started in December 2019. Three years of prolonged exposure to the COVID-19 pandemic and restrictive quarantine policy had a notable impact on the mental health of frontline nurses.

pmc-11635102.title: Transcriptome and Evolutionary Analysis of Pseudotrichomonas keilini, a Free-Living Anaerobic Eukaryote
pmc-11635102.creator: Hend Abu-Elmakarem, Stephen J Taerum, Celine Petitjean, Michael Kotyk, Christopher Kay, Ivan Čepička, David Bass, Gillian H Gile, Tom A Williams
pmc-11635102.description: The early evolution of eukaryotes and their adaptations to low-oxygen environments are fascinating open questions in biology. Genome-scale data from novel eukaryotes, and particularly from free-living lineages, are the key to answering these questions. The Parabasalia are a major group of anaerobic eukaryotes that form the most speciose lineage of Metamonada.

pmc-12404820.title: Prior hip arthroscopy impacts long-term outcomes of total hip arthroplasty
pmc-12404820.creator: Roger Quesada-Jimenez, Elizabeth G Walsh, Ady H Kahana-Rojkind, Drashti Sikligar, Krishi Rana, Benjamin G Domb
pmc-12404820.description: AimsThe objective of this study was to perform a long-term comparative analysis of patients who underwent total hip arthroplasty (THA) with a history of previous ipsilateral hip arthroscopy (PA) to a propensity-score matched control group of primary THA with no prior hip arthroscopy (NPA).

pmc-13101036.title: Distinct Host Gene Expression Patterns Induced by Covert Deformed Wing Virus Infections in Honeybees (Apis mellifera)
pmc-13101036.creator: Ali Sinan Kara, Samet Okuyan, Hatice Nur Kaynak, Serap Sakarya, Zeynep Ebrar Yavuz, Salim Aktürk, Gökhan Akdeniz, Aydin Turkec, Stuart J Lucas
pmc-13101036.description: Deformed Wing Virus (DWV) is a widespread insect pathogen and a major contributor to honeybee colony losses. While overt infections cause characteristic deformities and behavioral changes, covert or low‐level infections remain poorly understood. Here, we hypothesize that nonsymptomatic DWV infections induce distinct host transcriptional responses compared to symptomatic cases, which may influence the ultimate outcome of infection.
